bug_semantics: Authenticated IDOR (CWE-639) in web/html/funcionario/profile_funcionario.php: $id_pessoa is taken from $_SESSION['id_pessoa'], then extract($_REQUEST) overwrites that local with an attacker-supplied id_pessoa query/body parameter. The subsequent prepared query SELECT adm_configurado FROM pessoa WHERE id_pessoa=:idPessoa binds the overwritten $id_pessoa, so any logged-in user who can open an employee profile can read another person's administrative flag by enumerating id_pessoa. A later cargo-hierarchy check compares the target employee to the same overwritten $id_pessoa, so the identifier spoof also distorts self-vs-other authorization. The employee row itself is still selected via id_funcionario; the IDOR sink is the session-derived person id used after extract. Vendor first-party GHSA-jqh5-66qr-85qv (published, not withdrawn) and CVE-2026-76634 (CVE.org state PUBLISHED, not rejected) describe this overwrite. Affected first-party range is <=3.9.1, patched in 3.9.2.
flaw_origin: The unsafe extract($_REQUEST) call had existed at the top of profile_funcionario.php since 81e82f2d9deb7c060d9c29954ecb202d52c9c42b (2021-10-15), but the adm_configurado lookup used $_SESSION['id_pessoa'] directly, so injecting id_pessoa did not retarget that query. BIC c881b4e14637b3fb5c91168bcdb6bfea4d778dde (2025-12-18, Issue #1182 CSRF work) first wrote $id_pessoa = filter_var($_SESSION['id_pessoa'], ...) immediately before the pre-existing extract($_REQUEST), then changed the query to bindValue(':idPessoa', $id_pessoa). That is the first public-history write of the session-then-extract-then-query overwrite. The commit is a single-parent human edit, not a move, revert, or squash.
